chapters.title: God creates the heaven and the earth

parts.text: God creates the heaven and the earth and brings order through his word. During the first four days, he separates light from darkness, divides the waters, gathers the seas so dry land appears, brings forth vegetation, and appoints lights to mark days, seasons, and years.

On the fifth and sixth days, God creates creatures of the waters, birds, and land animals. He makes man, male and female, in his own image, blesses them, and gives them dominion over the living creatures. He commands them to multiply and fill the earth, provides food for people and animals, and declares everything he has made very good.

chapters.title: The garden and the first marriage

parts.text: God finishes his work, rests on the seventh day, and blesses and sanctifies it. The account then describes the LORD God forming man from the dust and breathing life into him. He places the man in the garden of Eden to tend and keep it. Among its trees are the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; eating from the latter is forbidden on pain of death.

God says it is not good for the man to be alone. Adam names the animals, but no suitable companion is found for him. God forms a woman from Adam’s rib and brings her to him. The chapter establishes the joining of husband and wife as one flesh; both are naked and unashamed.

chapters.title: Disobedience and departure from Eden

parts.text: The serpent contradicts God’s warning about the forbidden fruit. The woman eats and gives some to her husband, who also eats. Aware of their nakedness, they make coverings and hide from God. When questioned, Adam points to the woman, and she says the serpent deceived her.

God pronounces judgment on the serpent, including enmity between its seed and the woman’s seed. He declares sorrow in childbearing, a changed relationship between husband and wife, and painful labour on cursed ground until man returns to dust. Adam names his wife Eve. God clothes them with skins and sends them out of Eden, placing cherubims and a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life.

chapters.title: Cain, Abel, and their family lines

parts.text: Cain brings produce to the LORD, while Abel brings firstlings of his flock. God accepts Abel and his offering but not Cain and his. Despite God’s warning about sin, Cain kills his brother. God confronts him and makes him a fugitive and wanderer, yet places a mark on him to protect him from being killed.

Cain’s descendants include city builders and pioneers in keeping livestock, music, and metalworking. Lamech takes two wives and speaks of killing a man and claiming vengeance beyond Cain’s. Adam and Eve have another son, Seth, whom Eve regards as appointed in Abel’s place. After Seth’s son Enos is born, men begin to call upon the name of the LORD.

chapters.title: From Adam to Noah

parts.text: The genealogy traces Adam’s line through Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel, and Jared. It records the men’s ages at the birth of the named sons, their further children, their long lifespans, and their deaths. Adam lives 930 years.

Enoch stands out: he walks with God, and God takes him. His son Methuselah lives 969 years. Lamech names his son Noah in the hope of comfort from the toil connected with the ground the LORD has cursed. The chapter ends by introducing Noah’s sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

chapters.title: Corruption and the command to build an ark

parts.text: As mankind multiplies, the sons of God take wives from the daughters of men, and the chapter mentions giants and mighty men of renown. Human wickedness becomes great, and the earth is filled with corruption and violence. God is grieved and declares judgment, but Noah finds grace in his eyes and is described as a just man who walks with God.

God tells Noah that a flood will destroy life upon the earth and gives him instructions for building an ark of gopher wood. He promises to establish his covenant with Noah, who is to enter with his wife, sons, and their wives. Animals and food are to be brought aboard to preserve life. Noah does all that God commands.

chapters.title: The flood covers the earth

parts.text: The LORD tells Noah to enter the ark with his household, taking clean animals and birds by sevens and unclean animals by twos. After seven days, the flood begins: the fountains of the great deep break open and the windows of heaven are opened, bringing forty days and nights of rain. Noah’s family and the animals enter, and the LORD shuts him in.

The rising waters lift the ark. The flood covers even the high mountains. All land creatures and people outside the ark die; Noah and those with him remain alive. The waters prevail upon the earth for 150 days.

chapters.title: The waters recede and Noah leaves the ark

parts.text: God remembers Noah and the creatures in the ark, sends a wind, and causes the waters to recede. The ark rests on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sends out a raven and then a dove; the dove eventually returns with an olive leaf, and on a later flight does not return. In time, the ground becomes dry.

At God’s command, Noah’s family and the animals leave the ark to multiply upon the earth. Noah builds an altar and offers burnt offerings from clean animals and birds. The LORD receives the offering and resolves not to smite every living thing again as he has done. While the earth remains, its seasons and the cycle of day and night will continue.

chapters.title: God’s covenant and Noah’s household

parts.text: God blesses Noah and his sons and commands them to multiply. He permits meat for food but forbids eating its blood, and requires an accounting for the shedding of human blood because man is made in God’s image. He establishes a covenant with Noah’s descendants and every living creature: a flood will never again destroy all flesh. The bow in the cloud is its token.

Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk, and lies uncovered in his tent. Ham sees his father’s nakedness and tells his brothers; Shem and Japheth cover Noah without looking. When Noah learns what happened, he curses Canaan and speaks blessings concerning Shem and Japheth. Noah dies at 950 years old.

chapters.title: The families and nations after the flood

parts.text: The chapter records the descendants of Noah’s sons and the peoples who spread from them. Japheth’s line is associated with the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands. Ham’s descendants include Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan. Cush’s son Nimrod becomes a mighty hunter, and the beginning of his kingdom includes Babel in Shinar. Canaan’s descendants and their territory are also described.

Shem’s line includes Eber and his sons Peleg and Joktan. Peleg’s name is connected with the division of the earth in his days, while Joktan’s descendants are listed with their dwelling places. The nations are presented according to their families, languages, lands, and descent from Noah after the flood.

chapters.title: Babel and the family of Abram

parts.text: With one common language, people settle in Shinar and build a city and a tower reaching toward heaven. They want to make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered. The LORD confounds their language so they cannot understand one another, scatters them across the earth, and they stop building the city. It is called Babel.

A genealogy follows Shem’s line through Arphaxad to Terah, the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran dies, leaving his son Lot. Abram marries Sarai, who has no child. Terah takes Abram, Sarai, and Lot from Ur of the Chaldees toward Canaan, but they settle in Haran, where Terah dies.

chapters.title: Abram’s call and journey into Egypt

parts.text: The LORD calls Abram to leave his country and kindred for a land he will show him. He promises to make Abram a great nation, bless him, and bless all families of the earth through him. Abram leaves at seventy-five with Sarai and Lot. In Canaan, God promises the land to his seed, and Abram builds altars and calls upon the LORD.

A famine takes Abram into Egypt. Fearing that he will be killed because of Sarai’s beauty, he asks her to say she is his sister. She is taken into Pharaoh’s house, and Abram receives gifts. The LORD plagues Pharaoh’s household; Pharaoh rebukes Abram, restores Sarai, and sends them away.

chapters.title: Abram and Lot separate

parts.text: Abram returns from Egypt with Sarai, Lot, and great possessions, and again calls upon the LORD near Beth-el. Their flocks become too large for them to remain together, and their herdmen quarrel. Abram offers Lot the first choice of land to avoid strife. Lot chooses the well-watered plain of Jordan and pitches his tent toward Sodom, whose inhabitants are exceedingly wicked.

After Lot departs, the LORD tells Abram to look in every direction: the land will belong to him and his seed for ever, and his descendants will be as numerous as the dust of the earth. Abram moves to the plain of Mamre at Hebron and builds an altar.

chapters.title: Abram rescues Lot

parts.text: A war between kings brings defeat to Sodom and Gomorrah, and Lot is carried away with their goods. Abram hears of his nephew’s capture and pursues the victors with 318 trained servants and his allies. A night attack defeats them, and Abram recovers Lot, the other captives, and the goods.

Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram, praising God for the victory. Abram gives him tithes of all. When the king of Sodom offers Abram the recovered goods, Abram refuses to enrich himself from them, so the king cannot claim to have made him rich. He allows for his men’s food and his allies’ shares.

chapters.title: God confirms his covenant with Abram

parts.text: The LORD tells Abram not to fear and promises to be his shield and reward. Abram asks about his lack of an heir. God says that Abram’s own son will inherit and compares his descendants to the stars. Abram believes the LORD, who counts it to him for righteousness.

God directs Abram to prepare animals for a covenant. In a deep sleep, Abram hears that his descendants will be strangers, servants, and afflicted for four hundred years, but God will judge their oppressors and bring them out with great possessions. They will return when the time of the Amorites’ iniquity is complete. A smoking furnace and burning lamp pass between the pieces, and God promises the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.

chapters.title: Hagar and the birth of Ishmael

parts.text: Still childless, Sarai gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram as a wife so she may obtain children through her. Hagar conceives and begins to despise Sarai. Conflict follows, and after Sarai deals harshly with her, Hagar flees.

The angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a fountain in the wilderness and tells her to return and submit to Sarai. He promises numerous descendants and instructs her to name her son Ishmael because the LORD has heard her affliction. He also describes the strife that will characterize Ishmael’s life. Hagar acknowledges the God who sees her. She bears Ishmael when Abram is eighty-six.

chapters.title: New names and the sign of the covenant

parts.text: When Abram is ninety-nine, God appears as Almighty God and tells him to walk before him and be perfect. He confirms an everlasting covenant, promises nations and kings from him, and changes his name to Abraham. Canaan is promised as an everlasting possession. Circumcision is appointed as the covenant’s token for every male in his household and descendants.

God changes Sarai’s name to Sarah and promises that she will bear Isaac, through whom the covenant will be established. Abraham laughs at the thought of a son in their old age and pleads for Ishmael. God promises to bless Ishmael with twelve princes and a great nation, while distinguishing Isaac as the covenant son. Abraham circumcises himself, Ishmael, and every male of his household that same day.

chapters.title: The promised son and Abraham’s intercession

parts.text: The LORD appears to Abraham at Mamre, where Abraham welcomes three visitors and prepares a meal. The promise that Sarah will bear a son is repeated. Hearing it, Sarah laughs within herself because of their old age. The LORD asks why she laughed and declares that nothing is too hard for him.

The LORD speaks of Abraham’s future and his responsibility to teach his household righteousness and judgment, then reveals the grave outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah. As the men go toward Sodom, Abraham asks whether the righteous will be destroyed with the wicked. He appeals successively from fifty righteous people down to ten. The LORD agrees not to destroy the city if ten are found there.

chapters.title: Lot escapes the destruction of Sodom

parts.text: Two angels enter Sodom, and Lot receives them into his home. The men of the city surround the house and demand the visitors for sexual abuse. Lot offers his daughters instead, but the mob threatens him. The angels pull him inside, strike the attackers with blindness, and warn that the city will be destroyed. Lot’s sons-in-law do not take his warning seriously.

The angels lead Lot, his wife, and two daughters out. Lot reaches Zoar before the LORD rains fire and brimstone on Sodom and Gomorrah. His wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. God remembers Abraham and brings Lot out of the overthrow.
Later, in a cave, Lot’s daughters make him drunk and become pregnant by him to preserve their family line. Their sons, Moab and Ben-ammi, become the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.

chapters.title: Abraham and Sarah in Gerar

parts.text: In Gerar, Abraham again describes Sarah as his sister, and King Abimelech takes her. Before he touches her, God warns him in a dream that she is married. Abimelech pleads his innocence, and God says he has kept him from sinning. He must restore Sarah, and Abraham will pray for him.

Abimelech rebukes Abraham for bringing danger upon his kingdom. Abraham explains his fear of being killed and says Sarah is also his half-sister. Abimelech returns her, gives gifts, and permits Abraham to dwell in the land. Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech’s household, whose women had been prevented from bearing children because of Sarah.

chapters.title: Isaac is born; Hagar and Ishmael depart

parts.text: The LORD fulfils his promise, and Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is a hundred years old. Abraham circumcises him on the eighth day. Sarah rejoices that God has given her laughter, and Abraham holds a feast when Isaac is weaned.

After seeing Hagar’s son mocking, Sarah asks Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away. God tells Abraham to listen to Sarah, confirms Isaac’s place in the promised line, and promises to make Ishmael a nation also. In the wilderness, their water runs out, but God hears the boy and shows Hagar a well. Ishmael grows up in Paran.
Abimelech seeks an agreement with Abraham, recognizing that God is with him. They settle a dispute over a well and make a covenant at Beer-sheba, where Abraham calls upon the everlasting God.

chapters.title: Abraham is tested

parts.text: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac in the land of Moriah. Abraham obeys, travelling with Isaac and two servants. As they approach the place, Isaac asks about the lamb, and Abraham says God will provide. Abraham builds an altar, binds Isaac, and raises the knife, but the angel of the LORD stops him. A ram caught in a thicket is offered instead, and Abraham names the place Jehovah-jireh.

The LORD confirms by an oath the promises of abundant descendants, victory over enemies, and blessing to all nations through Abraham’s seed because he has obeyed. Abraham returns to Beer-sheba. News of his brother Nahor’s descendants introduces Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel.

chapters.title: Sarah’s death and a burial place

parts.text: Sarah dies at Hebron at 127 years old, and Abraham mourns her. Calling himself a stranger and sojourner, he asks the sons of Heth for a burial possession. He requests Ephron’s cave of Machpelah and insists on paying rather than accepting the property as a gift. In the presence of witnesses, he weighs out four hundred shekels of silver.

The field, its cave, and its trees are established as Abraham’s possession. He buries Sarah in the cave before Mamre. The chapter carefully records the public purchase and transfer of this burial place in the land of Canaan.

chapters.title: A wife is found for Isaac

parts.text: Abraham sends his chief servant to his kindred to find Isaac a wife, forbidding a Canaanite marriage and Isaac’s return to that country. At a well near Nahor’s city, the servant asks God for a sign: the chosen woman will offer water both to him and to his camels. Rebekah does exactly this. Learning that she is Abraham’s relative, he worships the LORD for guiding him.

At her family’s house, the servant recounts his mission and answered prayer before eating. Laban and Bethuel acknowledge the LORD’s direction and agree to the marriage. When the family asks for a delay, Rebekah herself agrees to go with the servant. They send her away with a blessing.
Rebekah travels to Canaan and meets Isaac, who has gone into the field to meditate. Isaac takes her as his wife, loves her, and is comforted after his mother’s death.

chapters.title: Abraham’s death and the birthright

parts.text: Abraham has further sons through Keturah, gives gifts to the sons of his concubines, and leaves his possessions to Isaac. He dies at 175, and Isaac and Ishmael bury him beside Sarah. God blesses Isaac. Ishmael’s descendants are listed as twelve princes, and his death at 137 is recorded.

Isaac prays for childless Rebekah, and she conceives twins. God tells her that two nations are in her womb and the elder will serve the younger. Esau becomes a hunter; Jacob dwells in tents. Returning hungry, Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and pottage of lentiles. The chapter concludes that Esau despised his birthright.

chapters.title: God’s promise to Isaac and disputes over wells

parts.text: During a famine, God tells Isaac to remain in the land rather than go to Egypt. He renews the promises made to Abraham concerning descendants, land, and blessing to all nations. In Gerar, Isaac calls Rebekah his sister out of fear. Abimelech discovers that she is his wife, rebukes Isaac, and orders the people not to harm them.

The LORD greatly prospers Isaac, provoking the Philistines’ envy. After being sent away, Isaac reopens Abraham’s wells and moves on from disputed wells until he finds room at Rehoboth. At Beer-sheba, God reassures him, and Isaac builds an altar. Abimelech seeks a covenant of peace with him. The chapter closes with Esau’s marriages to two Hittite women, which grieve Isaac and Rebekah.

chapters.title: Jacob receives Isaac’s blessing

parts.text: The aged Isaac asks Esau to hunt and prepare a meal before receiving his blessing. Rebekah overhears and arranges for Jacob to take Esau’s place, using prepared food, Esau’s clothes, and goatskins on Jacob’s hands and neck. Jacob claims to be Esau. Although Isaac questions the voice, he is deceived and blesses Jacob with abundance and authority over peoples and his brothers.

Esau returns and discovers what has happened. Isaac trembles but confirms the blessing already given. Esau weeps and receives words concerning life by the sword, service to his brother, and eventual release from his yoke. Esau plans to kill Jacob after Isaac’s death. Rebekah urges Jacob to flee to Laban and tells Isaac her concern that Jacob might marry a local woman.

chapters.title: Jacob’s dream at Beth-el

parts.text: Isaac sends Jacob to Padan-aram to marry one of Laban’s daughters, blesses him, and invokes Abraham’s blessing upon him and his descendants. Seeing that Canaanite wives displease his father, Esau takes a daughter of Ishmael as another wife.

On the journey, Jacob sleeps with a stone for his pillow and dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven, with angels ascending and descending. The LORD promises him the land, numerous descendants, blessing for all families through his seed, and protection until his return. Jacob wakes in awe, sets up and anoints the stone, and names the place Beth-el. He vows that if God keeps him and brings him home in peace, the LORD will be his God, and he will give a tenth of all God gives him.

chapters.title: Jacob marries Leah and Rachel

parts.text: Jacob reaches the land of his relatives, meets Rachel at a well, and helps water Laban’s flock. Laban welcomes him into his household. Jacob loves Rachel and agrees to serve seven years for her; the years seem only a few days because of his love.

At the marriage feast, Laban gives Jacob Leah instead. When Jacob discovers the deception, Laban appeals to the custom of marrying the elder daughter first. After Leah’s bridal week, Jacob receives Rachel also and serves another seven years. He loves Rachel more than Leah. The LORD sees Leah’s rejection and gives her children, while Rachel remains barren. Leah bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, expressing her hopes and praise in their names.

chapters.title: Jacob’s growing family and flocks

parts.text: Rachel, distressed by childlessness, gives Jacob her maid Bilhah, who bears Dan and Naphtali. Leah gives him Zilpah, who bears Gad and Asher. The sisters’ rivalry includes an exchange involving Reuben’s mandrakes and a night with Jacob. Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah. God then remembers Rachel, hears her, and gives her Joseph.

Jacob asks to leave, but Laban wants him to stay because the LORD has blessed him for Jacob’s sake. They agree that specified spotted, speckled, and brown animals will be Jacob’s wages. Laban separates the existing animals of those kinds. Jacob uses peeled rods at the watering places, separates his own flocks, and favours the stronger animals in breeding. His flocks and possessions increase greatly.

chapters.title: Jacob leaves Laban

parts.text: As Laban’s household grows resentful of Jacob’s prosperity, the LORD tells Jacob to return home. Jacob explains to Rachel and Leah how their father changed his wages and how God protected and prospered him. They agree to leave. Jacob departs secretly with his family and possessions, unaware that Rachel has stolen Laban’s images.

Laban pursues, but God warns him in a dream concerning his treatment of Jacob. Laban challenges the secret departure and searches for his gods. Rachel hides them and prevents their discovery. Jacob recounts twenty years of hard service, bearing losses and enduring repeated changes in wages, and credits God with preventing his being sent away empty.

They make a covenant, marking it with a pillar and a heap of stones. They agree not to cross the boundary to harm each other, and Jacob is charged not to mistreat Laban’s daughters. After a shared meal, Laban blesses his family and departs.

chapters.title: Jacob prepares to meet Esau

parts.text: Angels of God meet Jacob, and he names the place Mahanaim. He sends messengers to Esau and learns that Esau is coming with four hundred men. Afraid, Jacob divides his company, prays for deliverance, recalls God’s promise, and acknowledges his unworthiness of God’s kindness. He sends successive groups of animals as gifts to appease Esau.

After sending his family across the Jabbok, Jacob remains alone and wrestles with a man until daybreak. His thigh is put out of joint, but he holds on and asks for a blessing. He receives the name Israel and a blessing. Jacob names the place Peniel, saying he has seen God face to face and his life is preserved. He leaves limping.

chapters.title: Jacob and Esau are reconciled

parts.text: Jacob approaches Esau with his household and bows seven times. Esau runs to embrace and kiss him, and both weep. Jacob introduces his family and urges Esau to accept the gift he sent, acknowledging God’s gracious provision. Esau initially declines but eventually accepts.

Esau offers to accompany Jacob or leave men with him. Jacob declines, explaining that the children and livestock need a slower pace. Esau returns to Seir, while Jacob journeys to Succoth and builds a house and shelters for his animals. Later, in the region of Shechem, Jacob buys the field where he pitches his tent and erects an altar called El-elohe-Israel.

chapters.title: Dinah and the violence at Shechem

parts.text: Shechem, the son of Hamor, takes and defiles Dinah, then seeks to marry her. Her brothers are grieved and angry. Hamor proposes intermarriage, settlement, and trade between the two households, while Shechem offers whatever marriage payment they require.

Jacob’s sons answer deceitfully, agreeing only if every male of the city is circumcised. Hamor and Shechem persuade the townsmen. On the third day, while they are sore, Simeon and Levi kill the males, including Hamor and Shechem, and take Dinah home. Jacob’s sons plunder the city and take women and children captive. Jacob rebukes Simeon and Levi for endangering the household; they answer by protesting the treatment of their sister.

chapters.title: Return to Beth-el and losses in Jacob’s family

parts.text: God tells Jacob to return to Beth-el and build an altar. Jacob has his household put away strange gods, cleanse themselves, and change their garments. God’s terror keeps neighbouring cities from pursuing them. At Beth-el, Rebekah’s nurse Deborah dies. God appears again, confirms Jacob’s name as Israel, and renews the promises of nations, kings, and the land.

Rachel dies while giving birth on the way to Ephrath, which is Beth-lehem. She names the child Ben-oni, but Jacob calls him Benjamin and marks Rachel’s grave with a pillar. Reuben lies with Bilhah, and Israel hears of it. The twelve sons are listed. Jacob comes to Isaac at Mamre; Isaac’s death at 180 and his burial by Esau and Jacob are recorded.

chapters.title: Esau’s descendants and the rulers of Edom

parts.text: The genealogy identifies Esau with Edom and records his wives, sons, grandsons, and the dukes descended from them. Esau settles in mount Seir, separating from Jacob because their combined possessions and livestock are too great for the land to support them together. Amalek is included among Esau’s descendants.

The chapter also lists the families and dukes of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the region. It then records the succession of kings who ruled Edom before any king ruled the children of Israel, followed by a further list of Edomite dukes and their dwelling places.

chapters.title: Joseph is sold into Egypt

parts.text: Seventeen-year-old Joseph brings his father a bad report about his brothers. Jacob loves him more than his other sons and gives him a coat of many colours. Joseph’s dreams of his brothers’ sheaves and the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him increase their hatred and envy. His father rebukes him but keeps the matter in mind.

Sent to check on his brothers, Joseph finds them at Dothan. They plan to kill him, but Reuben persuades them to put him in a pit, intending to rescue him later. Judah proposes selling him instead. Joseph is sold for twenty pieces of silver and taken to Egypt.
The brothers dip Joseph’s coat in goat’s blood and send it to Jacob, who concludes that a beast has killed him and mourns deeply. In Egypt, Joseph is sold to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s officer.

chapters.title: Judah and Tamar

parts.text: Judah has three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. Er marries Tamar, but the LORD kills him for his wickedness. Onan is told to raise offspring for his dead brother, yet deliberately prevents it; the LORD kills him also. Judah sends Tamar back to her father’s house to wait for Shelah.

After Judah’s wife dies, Tamar sees that Shelah is grown but has not been given to her. She disguises herself, and Judah mistakes her for a harlot. She conceives by him and keeps his signet, bracelets, and staff as a pledge. When her pregnancy becomes known, Judah orders her burned. She produces the pledge, and Judah acknowledges both his paternity and his failure toward her. Tamar bears twins, Pharez and Zarah; Zarah’s hand appears first, but Pharez is born first.

chapters.title: Joseph’s faithfulness and imprisonment

parts.text: In Egypt, the LORD is with Joseph and prospers him in Potiphar’s service. Potiphar places him over his household, which is blessed for Joseph’s sake. Potiphar’s wife tries to persuade Joseph to lie with her, but he refuses, calling it a great wickedness and sin against God.

When she repeatedly pressures him and finally catches his garment, Joseph leaves it in her hand and flees. She uses the garment to support a false accusation against him. Potiphar becomes angry and puts Joseph in prison. Even there, the LORD shows Joseph mercy and gives him favour with the keeper, who entrusts the prisoners and their work to him.

chapters.title: The butler’s and baker’s dreams

parts.text: Pharaoh’s chief butler and chief baker are imprisoned, and Joseph serves them. They each have a troubling dream on the same night. Joseph says interpretations belong to God. He explains that the butler’s three vine branches represent three days, after which he will be restored to office. Joseph asks him to remember his unjust imprisonment and speak to Pharaoh.

The baker describes three baskets on his head, with birds eating from the uppermost. Joseph says he will be hanged within three days and the birds will eat his flesh. On Pharaoh’s birthday, both interpretations come true: the butler is restored and the baker is hanged. The butler, however, forgets Joseph.

chapters.title: Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s dreams and governs Egypt

parts.text: Two years later, Pharaoh dreams of seven lean kine devouring seven fat kine, and seven thin ears of corn swallowing seven full ears. His wise men cannot explain them. The butler remembers Joseph, who is brought from prison. Joseph credits God with the answer: both dreams announce seven years of plenty followed by seven years of severe famine. Their repetition shows that the matter is established by God and will soon occur.

Joseph advises storing a fifth of the produce during the plentiful years. Pharaoh recognizes his wisdom and appoints him over Egypt, second only to himself. Joseph marries Asenath and begins his service at thirty. During the plentiful years he gathers immense supplies and has two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
The plentiful years end, and the famine begins as foretold. Joseph opens the storehouses and sells grain. People from other countries also come to Egypt for food.

chapters.title: Joseph’s brothers make their first journey to Egypt

parts.text: Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt for grain but keeps Benjamin at home. They bow before Joseph without recognizing him. Joseph recognizes them, remembers his dreams, and accuses them of being spies. After three days in custody, he keeps Simeon and sends the others to bring Benjamin as proof of their story. Hearing them discuss their guilt over his suffering, Joseph turns aside and weeps.

Joseph supplies grain and secretly returns each man’s money in his sack. Its discovery frightens them. Back in Canaan, they tell Jacob that Benjamin must go to Egypt. Jacob grieves over Joseph’s loss and Simeon’s absence, and refuses to risk Benjamin, despite Reuben’s offer of his own two sons’ lives as a guarantee of Benjamin’s safe return.

chapters.title: Benjamin goes to Egypt

parts.text: As the famine continues, Judah insists that they cannot return for grain without Benjamin. He pledges himself as surety for his brother. Jacob reluctantly agrees, sending a gift and double money so the earlier payment can be returned. He asks God Almighty to grant them mercy.

Joseph brings the brothers to his house. Fearing trouble over the money, they explain it to his steward, who reassures them and brings out Simeon. Joseph asks about their father and is so moved at seeing Benjamin that he withdraws to weep. At the meal, the brothers are astonished to be seated in birth order. Benjamin receives five times as much food as the others.

chapters.title: The silver cup and Judah’s appeal

parts.text: Joseph orders his silver cup placed in Benjamin’s sack along with the grain money. After the brothers leave, his steward overtakes and accuses them. They deny theft, but the search reveals the cup in Benjamin’s sack. All return in distress. Judah offers that they become servants, but Joseph insists that only the man with the cup remain, while the others return to their father.

Judah recounts Jacob’s attachment to Benjamin and the grief caused by the loss of his other son. He says that returning without Benjamin would bring their father to the grave. Having pledged responsibility for Benjamin, Judah asks to remain as Joseph’s servant in his place rather than see the sorrow that would come upon Jacob.

chapters.title: Joseph makes himself known

parts.text: Joseph sends the attendants away, weeps aloud, and reveals his identity. His brothers are troubled, but he tells them not to be overwhelmed by their having sold him: God sent him ahead to preserve life. Two years of famine have passed, with five still to come. He urges them to bring Jacob and their households to Goshen, where he will provide for them. He embraces Benjamin and his other brothers.

Pharaoh approves the move and supplies wagons for the journey. Joseph sends provisions, gifts, and a warning not to quarrel on the way. Jacob at first cannot believe that Joseph is alive and ruling Egypt. After hearing Joseph’s words and seeing the wagons, his spirit revives, and he resolves to see his son before he dies.

chapters.title: Jacob’s household moves to Egypt

parts.text: On the journey, Jacob offers sacrifices at Beer-sheba. God speaks to him in the night, telling him not to fear going to Egypt: he will make him a great nation there, go with him, and bring him up again. Joseph will be with him at his death. Jacob’s family travels with their goods and livestock.

The chapter lists Jacob’s descendants by their mothers and gives the household total as seventy, including Joseph and his sons in Egypt. Jacob sends Judah ahead, and Joseph meets his father in Goshen, embracing him and weeping. Joseph prepares the family to tell Pharaoh that they are keepers of livestock, so they may dwell in Goshen apart from Egyptians, who regard shepherds as an abomination.

chapters.title: Life in Goshen and the famine’s cost

parts.text: Joseph presents five brothers and then Jacob to Pharaoh. Pharaoh permits the family to settle in the best of the land, and Jacob blesses him, describing his 130 years as few and troubled. Joseph settles and feeds his father’s household.

As the famine continues, Joseph receives the Egyptians’ money, then their livestock, and finally their land and service in exchange for food. The land becomes Pharaoh’s, except for the priests’ holdings. Joseph provides seed and establishes a requirement that a fifth of the harvest go to Pharaoh, with the rest kept for seed and household needs. The people acknowledge that he has preserved their lives.
Israel’s family prospers and multiplies in Goshen. After seventeen years in Egypt, Jacob requires Joseph to swear that he will bury him with his fathers rather than in Egypt.

chapters.title: Jacob blesses Ephraim and Manasseh

parts.text: Joseph brings his sons to the ailing Jacob. Recalling God’s promises at Luz, Jacob receives Ephraim and Manasseh as his own sons, giving them a place alongside Reuben and Simeon. He also recalls Rachel’s death. He rejoices that, having once thought Joseph lost, he has now seen Joseph’s children too.

Jacob crosses his hands, placing his right hand on the younger Ephraim and his left on Manasseh. He invokes the God who has cared for him and the Angel who redeemed him from evil. Joseph tries to correct the placement, but Jacob deliberately gives Ephraim the greater position, while promising greatness to both. He assures Joseph that God will bring the family back to their fathers’ land and gives him an additional portion.

chapters.title: Jacob’s final words to his sons

parts.text: Jacob gathers his sons to tell what will befall them in the last days. Reuben will not excel because he defiled his father’s bed. Simeon and Levi are condemned for cruel anger and will be scattered. Judah receives promises of his brothers’ praise and royal authority: the sceptre will not depart until Shiloh comes, to whom the people will gather.

Zebulun is associated with the sea; Issachar with burdens and tribute; Dan with judging and a serpent’s attack. Jacob expresses hope in the LORD’s salvation. Gad will be overcome but prevail at last; Asher will provide rich food; Naphtali is likened to a released hind and associated with good words.

Joseph is described as fruitful and strengthened by God amid attacks, receiving abundant blessings. Benjamin is likened to a ravening wolf. After blessing the twelve tribes, Jacob commands burial in Machpelah with Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah. He finishes speaking and dies.

chapters.title: Burial, forgiveness, and the promise of return

parts.text: Joseph mourns Jacob and has him embalmed. With Pharaoh’s permission, a large company accompanies the family to Canaan. They hold a further mourning at the threshingfloor of Atad and bury Jacob in the cave of Machpelah, as he commanded, before returning to Egypt.

The brothers fear that Joseph will now repay their wrongdoing. Joseph weeps, reassures them, and distinguishes their evil intention from God’s purpose to preserve many lives. He promises to provide for them and their children.

Joseph lives to 110 and sees later generations of his family. Before dying, he declares that God will visit Israel and bring them to the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He makes them swear to carry his bones with them. He is embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.
